set.body:
Found by the PLS Neuro basis-set review on 2026-09-11 and checked numerically by an independent reviewer. Revision a3ee73b.

What the code does:
- HrfFunctions.scala:77-83 spmg1Deriv is the analytic first time derivative of the canonical.
- HrfFunctions.scala:85-95 spmg1SecondDeriv is the analytic second time derivative.
- SPMG2 and SPMG3 bind these with bindBasis (HrfFunctions.scala:676-686), which only concatenates columns (Decorators.scala:38-57). Nothing in the hrf module orthogonalises.

What users expect: SPM's informed basis has a temporal derivative and a dispersion derivative (the derivative with respect to the response's dispersion parameter), both orthogonalised against the canonical. Anyone reading "SPMG3" or "dispersion derivative" assumes that.

Measured over 0-24 s:
- The first derivative is orthogonal to the canonical anyway, by integration by parts (<h,h'>/<h,h> = 2.4e-7). So for SPMG2 the canonical amplitude is beta1.
- corr(h, h'') = -0.51. So for SPMG3 the canonical-shape amplitude is beta1 - 0.112 * beta3, not beta1.
- The derivative is unnormalised: ||h'||^2 / ||h||^2 = 0.11. The textbook derivative-boosted amplitude sign(b1) * sqrt(b1^2 + b2^2) returns 1.33 and 1.72 for a true 1.0 shifted by 1 s and 2 s. Scaled by the L2 norms, it returns 0.996 and 0.953.

Decide:
(a) Name the third function for what it is ("second time derivative") in descriptors and basis roles, or implement SPM's dispersion derivative.
(b) Offer an orthogonalised variant (Gram-Schmidt against the canonical over a declared window), or document that the coefficients are not orthogonal.
(c) Normalise the derivatives, or document their scale.

Downstream: PLS Neuro labels this family "Canonical + time + dispersion" (glm-review-javafx ModelEditorPane.scala:32-38) and will rename it once this is decided.
set.title: SPMG2/3 derivatives are raw analytic d/dt and d2/dt2, not orthogonalised; the third function is not SPM's dispersion derivative
